newsitem.title: CANADA: NHL ICE HOCKEY - RANGERS FINALLY WIN ONE IN MONTREAL.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY - RANGERS FINALLY WIN ONE IN MONTREAL.

text.p: Luc Robitaille scored off Wayne Gretzky's centering pass 42 seconds into overtime, giving the surging New York Rangers their first regular-season win in Montreal in more than five years, 3-2 over the slumping Canadiens on Saturday.
Gretzky, who set up all three New York goals, had the puck behind the Montreal net and was left unchecked for several seconds before shoveling a shot past goaltender Jocelyn Thibault's stick side.

"(Gretzky) beat me on the winning goal the same way he beat me on the first two goals," a frustrated Thibault said. "He had a chance three times. You never know where he is or where he's going to pass the puck."

In Boston, Rob DiMaio scored his second goal of the game with 56 seconds remaining as the the Boston Bruins extended their winning streak to three games with a 4-3 victory over the Washington Capitals.
Washington tied it, 3-3, on Dale Hunter's goal 6:38 into the third.
But Jozef Stumpel fired a shot from the right faceoff circle and the rebound came out to Dimaio, who snapped the puck inside the left goalpost for his eighth goal.
Steve Staios and Sheldon Kennedy also scored for Boston.
In Hartford, Robert Kron's goal at 2:11 of overtime gave the Hartford Whalers a wild 6-5 victory over the Tampa Bay Lightning, who took their third straight loss.
"Basically, I just threw it at the net," Kron said. I knew he had been creeping off the post during the game and I wanted to make sure I got the shot on goal."
At the Islanders, Joe Nieuwendyk's goal with 1:45 remaining enabled the Dallas Stars to extend their unbeaten streak to a season-high seven games with a 3-2 triumph over the New York Islanders.

Nieuwendyk took a pass from Jamie Langenbrunner and split two defenders as he crossed the blue line. He turned defenceman Bryan Berard around, then fired a slap shot that hit the inside of goaltender Tommy Salo's right pad and slid into the net.

In Ottawa, Mike Peca scored the go-ahead goal 8:32 into the third period as the Buffalo Sabres survived a controversial finish to defeat the Ottawa Senators, 3-2 and extend their winning streak to four games.
With the game tied, 2-2, Peca stole a clearing pass from rookie defenceman Wade Redden, broke in from the blue line and and snapped a wrister past goaltender Damian Rhodes for his sixth goal.

In Philadelphia, Ron Hextall made 24 saves and Trent Klatt and Joel Otto scored second-period goals as the Philadelphia Flyers beat the St. Louis Blues, 4-0 for their fourth straight shutout and seventh straight victory.
The Flyers have not allowed a goal in more than 262 minutes.

"You don't get four shutouts in a row, I don't care who it is, you could be All-Universe, and there's still no way," Hextall said. "It's impossible in this league in this day and age, this is a team thing. When you get four in a row, it makes it special."

In Pittsburgh, rookie Patrick Lalime made 32 saves to remain unbeaten and red-hot Mario Lemieux had a goal and an assist as the Pittsburgh Penguins continued their dominance of the San Jose Sharks with a 3-1 victory.

Lalime made 16 saves in the first period, seven in the second and nine in the third to improve to 5-0. He was tested with five minutes left in the game, but kicked away Ulf Dahlen's slap shot from the slot.

At Colorado, Mats Sundin had his fifth career hat trick and rookie David Cooper scored his first NHL goal to lead the Toronto Maple Leafs to their second win in six games, 6-2 over the Colorado Avalanche.
Cooper, recalled from the minors a week ago, scored during a 5-on-3 power play when his wrist shot from the top of the right faceoff circle beat Patrick Roy at 7:31 of the first period.
